title: Can Digitalization Improve Public Services? Evidence from Innovation in Energy Management
eligible_reason: The underlying design is a textbook staggered binary adoption (utility-level smart-meter / AMI deployment, 7 adoption cohorts 2010-2016, 601 never-treated of 1,306 utilities, absorbing treatment, utility FE + state-by-year FE), but no published specification satisfies the rules: every main-text regression is the Freyaldenhoven-Hansen-Shapiro 'augmented' DiD estimated by ivreghdfe with a time-varying control (buildunits) and log population instrumented by the one-year lead of treatment (logpop = lead1AMI); the event studies (Figures 2-4) use xtevent with the same proxy/proxy-IV and control; Table 3 adds AMI x DP/DR interactions; Table 4 is an MSA-occupation-year regression of AMI x occupation-type interactions with MSA-year FE; Table 5 is a bootstrapped Poisson (ppmlhdfe) with controls. Appendix Table C2 (OLS) and Table C3 (csdid) also include buildunits and logpop as covariates. IV, time-varying controls and nonlinear models are excluded by PROTOCOL Section 2.
design_notes: Utility-year panel 2007-2018 from EIA Form 861 (Data/Analysis/EIA_Panel.dta; analysis sample incl==1 & winslr!=1: 15,580 utility-years, 1,306 utilities; 14,252 obs in the IV regressions because lead1AMI drops 2018). AMI = (DataYear >= AMIyear), absorbing (verified: no utility switches off). Cohorts: 2010 (99 utilities), 2011 (112), 2012 (62), 2013 (147), 2014 (66), 2015 (106), 2016 (113); 601 never-adopters. Outcomes: loss_rate (losses/disposition), logRevenue_tot, logrev_ps_tot (average price), logsales_total_pc, DP/DR adoption; continuous version p2ami (share of customers with AMI). FE: absorb(ID DataYear#statecode), cluster(ID). Sub-samples: avgprelpr >= Q1 (pre-treatment loss rate above first quartile), firsttwo != 1 (drop first three post years), ownership splits.
estimators_reported: augmented_did_iv (ivreghdfe, FHS 2019 proxy-IV) static (Tables 2, 3, 6, C1, C4, C8)
augmented_did_iv event study (xtevent proxy/proxyiv; Figures 2, 3, 4, D3, D4b/d, D5, D7, D8)
twfe_ols_with_time_varying_controls (reghdfe loss_rate AMI buildunits logpop; Table C2, Table C5, Figure D4a/c)
callaway_santanna with covariates (csdid ... buildunits logpop, method(dripw), never-treated and notyet; Table C3)
twfe with treatment x occupation interactions (Table 4, C6)
ineligible_specs_summary: C1a_Analyze_EIA_Main.do lines 143-175 (Table 2A), 193-225 (Table 2B, continuous), 253-286 (Table 3, interactions), 310-367 (Table 6), 384-470 (Figures 2-4, xtevent proxy IV): all IV + buildunits control. C1b_Analyze_EIA_Appendix.do lines 109-150 (Table C2 OLS with buildunits logpop), 178-212 (Table C3 csdid with buildunits logpop), 239-248 (Table C4 IV), 274-290 (Table C5 OLS with controls and interactions), 390-412 (Table C8 IV continuous), 503-933 (Figures D2-D8 xtevent with controls/IV). C2a/C2b (Table 4, C6): AMI x occupation-group interactions, absorb(MSAcode#laborcode MSAcode#DataYear). C3_Analyze_Texas.do (Table 5): ppmlhdfe with bootstrap.

data_files_note: Full package (1.2 GB) now extracted at ~/did_packages/mnsc/mnsc.2024.06349/: Data/Analysis/EIA_Panel.dta (19,849 utility-years, 107 variables, 13 MB), Labor_MSA_Occ.dta, Texas_Feeder_Reliability.dta; Data/Processed/* and Data/Raw/* (EIA-861, SEER population, building permits, OEWS, Texas PUC). Only the S&P Global SNL raw files are withheld (an intermediate Utility_Distribution.dta is provided). Stata logs of the authors' run in Log/. Note: at the time of screening the package was being re-downloaded (the earlier _archive zip was truncated), so the lead's regressions list for this suffix was regenerated mid-screen.
software_note: Stata 19.5 (reghdfe, ivreghdfe, csdid, xtevent, ppmlhdfe, estout, coefplot, binscatter) and R 4.4.1 (maps only).
screener_notes: No article text. Not eligible as published: the authors deliberately 'augment' the staggered DiD with a pre-trend proxy IV (log population instrumented by the lead of AMI) plus a building-permit control in every table and figure, and even the OLS and csdid appendix versions keep buildunits and logpop as covariates. If the lead decides to admit a controls-free TWFE counterpart constructed by the team (reghdfe loss_rate AMI, absorb(ID DataYear#statecode) cluster(ID) on EIA_Panel.dta with incl==1 & winslr!=1), the data and sample definitions are fully available and the design (7 cohorts, 601 never-treated, absorbing) is clean; but that specification does not appear in the paper.
